Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS AI 补全经历

Describe an important decision that you made

描述你做过的一个重大决定

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe an important decision that you made

  • What the decision was (这个决定是什么)
  • How you made your decision (你是怎么做这个决定的)
  • What the results of the decision were (这个决定的结果是什么)
  • And explain why it was important (并解释为什么它很重要)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe an important decision that you made

I'd like to talk about the decision to choose computer science as my major at university, which I made when I was filling in my college application forms in my final year of high school. The decision itself was pretty clear in the end, but getting there took a while. I'd loved computers since I was a kid, always playing around with them, and in high school I had an IT teacher who taught me some basic programming during lunch breaks. He told me that if I was that interested, I should seriously consider it as a career. So when it came to choosing a major, I did a lot of research online, compared different universities, and talked it over with my parents, who were supportive as long as I was sure about it. As for the results, I'd say they've been very positive so far. I enjoy most of my courses, I've picked up skills that feel genuinely useful, and I've even built a few small projects on my own. It's confirmed that I made the right call. The reason it was so important is that it basically decided my career path. Everything I study now, and probably the job I'll do later, flows from that one choice. Looking back, I think it was the first really big decision I made entirely for myself, and it taught me to trust my own interests.

我讲的是高考填志愿时选择计算机科学与技术专业这个决定。我从小就爱玩电脑，高中信息技术老师午休时教我基础编程，鼓励我考虑这个方向；报志愿时我上网查资料、对比学校，也和爸妈商量，他们支持我。结果很正面：课程喜欢、学到实用技能、还自己做了小项目。之所以重要，是因为它基本决定了我的职业方向，也是我第一次完全为自己做的重大决定。

Q2Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?

Yes, I think they do, though the decisions are important in a different way from adults'. For example, children often have to choose which subjects to focus on, or which hobbies to keep, and those choices can shape their interests for years. Having said that, I don't think children should carry the full weight of big decisions, because they lack experience. So I'd say they make important decisions, but usually with guidance from adults.

是的，孩子也会做重要决定，只是和成人的重要方式不同。比如选重点科目、保留哪个爱好，这些会影响兴趣好几年。但孩子缺乏经验，不该独自承担重大决定的分量，通常需要大人引导。

Q3What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?

I'd say the biggest one is choosing their further education path, whether to go to university, which major to pick, or whether to enter the workforce directly. In my country, this choice basically decides a person's career direction, so it carries a lot of pressure. Another important decision is where to live, since many teenagers move to bigger cities for study or work. These choices are hard because teenagers often don't know yet what they really want.

最大的决定是升学路径：上不上大学、选什么专业、还是直接工作。在我国这基本决定职业方向，压力很大。另一个是去哪生活，很多青少年会去大城市。难就难在青少年往往还不知道自己真正想要什么。

Q4Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?

Generally speaking, children usually turn to their parents first, because parents know them best and have more life experience. Teachers are also a common source of help, especially for academic decisions, since they see the child's strengths in a school setting. These days, I'd also say the internet plays a role, because children can research options themselves. Having said that, I think the most reliable advice still comes from people who know the child personally.

孩子一般先找父母，因为父母最了解他们、经验也更多。老师也常被求助，尤其学业决定，因为老师看得见孩子的长处。现在网络也起作用，孩子能自己查资料。但最可靠的建议还是来自真正了解孩子的人。

Q5Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?

Yes, I think advertisements influence us more than we realise. They work by creating desire, so when we see a product presented in an attractive way, we start to believe we need it. For example, in my country, online ads follow people around based on what they've searched, which makes it very hard to resist. Having said that, I think most people are becoming more aware of this, and they compare reviews before buying, so the influence isn't total.

是的，广告对我们的影响比想象中大。它通过制造欲望起作用，把产品包装得吸引人，我们就开始觉得需要它。比如国内线上广告会根据搜索记录追着人推，很难抗拒。但多数人越来越有意识，买前会看评价，所以影响不是绝对的。

Q6Do you think the influence of advertising is good?

I'd say it's a mixed picture. On one hand, advertising helps people discover new products and services, and it supports a lot of free content online, which is clearly beneficial. On the other hand, it can push people to buy things they don't need, and some ads are misleading. On balance, I think advertising itself is neutral, but it becomes a problem when it's dishonest or targets vulnerable people, like children. So the influence depends a lot on how it's used.

好坏参半。一方面广告帮人发现新产品、支撑大量免费内容，明显有益；另一方面会推着人买不需要的东西，有些广告还误导人。总体看广告本身是中性的，但一旦不诚实或针对儿童等弱势群体就成了问题，所以影响取决于怎么用。

Q7How do people usually make important decisions?

I think most people start by gathering information, so they research the options and compare the pros and cons. After that, many people ask for advice from family or friends, because a second opinion can reveal things they've missed. Some people also rely on their gut feeling, especially when the options seem equally good. Having said that, I believe the most sensible approach is a combination, using both careful analysis and personal instinct.

多数人先收集信息，查选项、对比利弊；然后会问家人朋友的意见，因为旁观者能看出自己漏掉的东西。也有人靠直觉，尤其当选项看起来差不多时。最明智的做法是两者结合：认真分析加个人直觉。
